_meta.title: Authored by-sign lunation cards (REVIEWED, needs sign-off)
_meta.principle: name the ordinary behavior first, then why it must change
_meta.note: Marie-voiced originals following the lunation surface templates; Full-Moon cards always name the house axis. Linted by tests/render_lunation_authored.py. Serve only after sign-off.

reviewed.text: The Full Moon lands in your 10th house, highlighting the 10th/4th house axis of public role versus private life. Something you've built in your career comes into full view now, and you feel the pull between what your work demands and what home actually needs. If you've been pouring everything into how you're seen and quietly letting the home front slide, this Full Moon makes the imbalance hard to miss. Your reputation is real and so is your exhaustion. The mars-uranus opposition may shake loose a work arrangement you thought was stable. This could be the moment to stop performing a steadiness you don't feel and admit which part of your life has been running on empty. You might be ready to let go of a version of success that costs you the place you come home to.

reviewed.text: The Full Moon lands in your 9th house, highlighting the 9th/3rd house axis of the big picture versus the daily details. A belief about where your life is headed comes to a head now, set against the smaller conversations and errands that fill your actual days. If you've been so buried in the day-to-day that you stopped asking whether any of it is taking you somewhere you want to go, this Full Moon raises the question out loud. Both the routine and the longing are valid. The mars-uranus opposition can jolt loose a fixed idea about what you're allowed to want. This is a good moment to name the bigger direction you've been treating as impractical, and to notice which daily habits quietly argue against it. You might be ready to release a story that says curiosity is a luxury you have to earn.
reviewed.review_note: authored Marie-voiced original; needs Marie/editorial sign-off

reviewed.text: The Full Moon lands in your 8th house, highlighting the 8th/2nd house axis of shared resources versus what is yours alone. Something about money, intimacy, or dependence on another person surfaces now, and it asks for more honesty than usual. If you've been avoiding a conversation about who owes what, or leaning on someone in a way that quietly costs you, this Full Moon pulls it into the open. Needing support is human and so is wanting your own footing. The mars-uranus opposition may disrupt an arrangement you've been tolerating. This could be the moment to look plainly at where your security is tangled up with someone else's, and to ask what you'd need to stand on your own. You might be ready to let go of a debt, financial or emotional, that you've carried well past its usefulness.
reviewed.review_note: authored Marie-voiced original; needs Marie/editorial sign-off

reviewed.text: The Full Moon lands in your 7th house, highlighting the 7th/1st house axis of partnership versus self. A close relationship reaches a point of clarity now, and the gap between who you are alone and who you become with someone else gets hard to ignore. If you've been shaping yourself around another person's moods to keep the peace, this Full Moon shows you the cost. Wanting the relationship and wanting yourself back can both be true. The mars-uranus opposition may crack open a dynamic that has felt stuck for a while. This is a good moment to say the honest thing you've been managing around, and to notice where you've traded your own needs for a calm that isn't real. You might be ready to release a version of togetherness that only works when you disappear.

reviewed.text: The Full Moon lands in your 6th house, highlighting the 6th/12th house axis of daily work versus rest. The state of your body and your routines comes into full view now, all the effort you've been spending and the recovery you've been skipping. If you've been treating rest as something to reach once the list is finally done, this Full Moon makes the running total impossible to ignore. Being useful matters and so does being a person who isn't depleted. The mars-uranus opposition may force a sudden change in your schedule or your health. This could be the moment to build recovery into the day on purpose instead of hoping to find it later. You might be ready to let go of the belief that your worth is measured in how much you get through.

reviewed.text: The Full Moon lands in your 5th house, highlighting the 5th/11th house axis of personal joy versus the wider group. Something about your own pleasure, a creative project, or a romance comes to a head now, set against your obligations to friends and the crowd you belong to. If you've been showing up for everyone's plans while your own creative life goes untended, this Full Moon makes the imbalance clear. Being a good friend and being a full person are both real. The mars-uranus opposition may shake up a friendship or a group you've quietly outgrown. This is a good moment to reclaim a little of the time you give away, and to notice which rooms leave you brighter and which just leave you tired. You might be ready to release a version of belonging that has no room for what actually delights you.

reviewed.text: The Full Moon lands in your 4th house, highlighting the 4th/10th house axis of home versus public life. Something at the root of your life, your family, where you live, the ground you stand on, comes into full view now, set against the demands of your career. If you've been so focused on the outer climb that the home front has quietly frayed, this Full Moon pulls it forward. Ambition is real and so is the need for a place that holds you. The mars-uranus opposition may unsettle your living situation or a family dynamic. This could be the moment to tend the foundation you've been treating as an afterthought, and to notice what you've been calling home that doesn't actually feel like one. You might be ready to let go of an old family script about what you owe and to whom.

reviewed.text: The Full Moon lands in your 3rd house, highlighting the 3rd/9th house axis of the daily mind versus the bigger picture. Something about how you think, talk, and move through your immediate world comes to a head now, set against the beliefs that are supposed to guide it. If you've been staying busy with messages, errands, and small talk to avoid a larger question about where you're going, this Full Moon surfaces it. The daily noise is real and so is the quiet you've been outrunning. The mars-uranus opposition can jolt loose a fixed opinion or a stalled conversation. This is a good moment to say the thing you've been circling, and to notice which mental habits keep you too occupied to think. You might be ready to release a story that keeps your world smaller than it needs to be.

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on your home, family, and the private base you build everything else on. You might be noticing where you've treated your living space and your family ties as the thing you'll get to once the real work is done. You learned somewhere that resting at home had to be earned, that softness was for after the fighting was over. But you can't launch from a base you never tend. This month, set one small intention for your home: a corner made comfortable, a gentle start to a hard family conversation, an evening that belongs to no one's demands. Plant it quietly and let it grow before you have anything to show for it.

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on your communication, learning, and the daily exchanges that make up your world. You might be noticing where you've gone quiet, keeping thoughts to yourself because saying them felt risky or not worth the trouble. Somewhere you decided it was safer to stay agreeable than to be fully understood. But the people close to you can only respond to the version of you that you actually voice. This month, set an intention to say one true thing you'd normally swallow, to ask the question you've been sitting on, or to start the conversation you keep rescheduling. It doesn't have to be perfect. It just has to be honest, and it just has to begin.

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on your values, money, and sense of your own worth. You might be noticing where you've been underselling yourself, taking the smaller ask, the lower rate, the leftover slice, because wanting more felt greedy or unsafe. Somewhere you learned that needing things put you at risk, so you got good at needing little. But a life built on going without slowly starves. This month, set an intention around worth: name one thing you actually want, ask for what your time is genuinely worth, or let yourself receive help without immediately paying it back. Start small, and let the sense that you're allowed to have needs take root.
reviewed.review_note: authored Marie-voiced original; needs Marie/editorial sign-off

reviewed.text: This New Moon lands in your own sign, focusing on your identity and how you begin again. You might be noticing where you've defined yourself entirely by who you take care of, so that without someone to tend, you're not quite sure who you are. Caretaking became your shape early, a way to stay needed and therefore safe. But you are allowed to exist as more than the person who holds everyone else together. This month, set an intention that's only about you: a want with no one else attached, a small act of self-tending, a beginning you don't have to justify. This is your New Moon. Let it be about the self you keep setting aside.

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on your inner life, rest, and what you're ready to release. You might be noticing how tired you are underneath the performance, how much energy goes into being on for everyone. Being visible and adored became proof that you mattered, so slowing down can feel like disappearing. But even the sun sets, and what recharges in the dark comes back brighter. This month, set a quiet intention that no one has to see: real rest, a private practice, or the release of something you've outgrown but kept performing anyway. You don't have to earn the pause. Let this be the beginning that happens off-stage.

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on your friendships, groups, and the future you're moving toward. You might be noticing where you've been the reliable one who organizes and fixes, quietly doing the group's emotional labor while your own needs go unspoken. Being useful became your ticket to belonging. But a circle that only wants your competence isn't the same as one that wants you. This month, set an intention around real connection: let a friend see you struggling, ask for help before you're drowning, or step toward a community that shares what you actually care about. Plant one honest bond and let it grow at its own pace.

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on your career and how you're known in the world. You might be noticing where you've shaped your public self around what others approve of, so that success feels strangely hollow when it arrives. Somewhere you learned that being liked was safer than being clear about what you want. But a reputation built on pleasing everyone can't hold anything that's truly yours. This month, set an intention about the work that matters to you: name an ambition out loud, take one step that's yours rather than expected, or let a little more of the real you into how you show up professionally. Start quietly, and let it build.

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on your beliefs, learning, and the wider horizon you've been circling. You might be noticing where you've kept your world tight and controlled, calling caution wisdom, because trusting something bigger felt dangerous. Depth has been your safety, but not everything worth knowing lives underground. This month, set an intention to expand on purpose: sign up for the thing you keep researching, book the trip you talk yourself out of, or let a new perspective actually change your mind. You don't have to see the whole path to take the first step onto it. Plant the curiosity and let it pull you somewhere new.

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on intimacy, trust, and the resources you share with others. You might be noticing where you keep things light to avoid the depth that real closeness asks for, laughing off the moments that want honesty instead. Staying free and unattached felt safer than being truly known. But the connection you actually crave lives on the other side of that guardedness. This month, set an intention around letting someone in: share a truth you'd normally keep to yourself, have the money or trust conversation you've been dodging, or let yourself depend on someone a little. Start with one honest moment and let the trust build from there.

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on your relationships and partnerships. You might be noticing where you've handled closeness like a project to manage, staying competent and a little walled off so no one sees you unsteady. Long ago, needing someone felt like a liability, so you learned to be the strong one who never asks. But partnership only works when both people are allowed to lean. This month, set an intention around softening: let a partner carry something for you, say the vulnerable thing instead of the composed one, or begin a relationship on more honest footing. You don't have to hold it all alone. Let this be where you practice being cared for.

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on your daily life, health, and the routines that carry you. You might be noticing where you've been running on a system that ignores your body, treating rest, food, and feeling as inefficiencies to override. Staying busy and detached kept difficult emotions at arm's length. But the body keeps its own record, and it eventually asks to be heard. This month, set an intention rooted in care rather than optimization: one routine that tends how you actually feel, a small daily kindness to your body, or a moment each day that isn't about being productive. Plant it gently and let a softer rhythm take hold.
reviewed.review_note: authored Marie-voiced original; needs Marie/editorial sign-off

reviewed.text: This New Moon focuses on your creativity, joy, and the things you make just because they're yours. You might be noticing where you've let your imagination go unused, waiting for permission or for it to be useful before you'll take it seriously. Somewhere you learned that play was frivolous, that dreaming didn't count as real. But joy is part of what makes the rest of life bearable, and it's allowed to come first sometimes. This month, set an intention around delight: make something with no purpose, follow a spark of inspiration without a plan, or let yourself want something purely because it's beautiful. Start small, and let the joy be reason enough.
